title: Last Day Where You Can Still Cross
summary: Given a 1-based binary matrix where land is 0 and water is 1, and a 1-based 2D array indicating when cells turn to water, find the last day one can walk from the top to the bottom on land.
statement: Given a 1-based binary matrix where land is 0 and water is 1, and a 1-based 2D array indicating when cells turn to water, find the last day one can walk from the top to the bottom on land. The walk can start from any top cell and end at any bottom cell, moving only in the four cardinal directions.
constraints: 2 <= row,col <= 20000, row*col <= 20000, and cells is a permutation of every 1-based grid coordinate.
On day d, the first d cells are water; movement uses four directions through land.
Return the greatest day when some top-row land cell connects to some bottom-row land cell.
hints: Crossability is monotone: once flooding disconnects top from bottom, later days cannot restore a path.
Binary-search the last feasible day; each check floods the prefix and runs multi-source BFS from all dry top cells.
can_cross(d): BFS four-direction land after first d floods; upper-bound binary search over 0..row*col.
BFS exactly recognizes a land connection, and monotonic flooding partitions days into feasible then infeasible, so upper-bound search returns the last feasible day.
editorial: BFS exactly recognizes a land connection, and monotonic flooding partitions days into feasible then infeasible, so upper-bound search returns the last feasible day.

tests.explanation: A right-column path remains on day two, but no crossing remains on day three.
Flooding both top cells takes two days, so day one is the last crossing day.
